# Retained ClickHouse merchant releases

Use the original seller release store to retain, compare, activate, drain and
roll back an existing [ClickHouse merchant](../sf30-seller-sdk/clickhouse/README.md).
The same original seller handles its HTTP 402 responses, native facilitator,
typed input validation, paid queries, operations and availability controls.

Each release keeps the original prepared source, plan, bindings, service,
OpenAPI and generated customer client. The original working directory can move
after staging. Connection values remain in the launching process environment;
the package contains only the selected environment variable names.

ClickHouse remains a live external database. Rollback restores the retained
query, input contract, payment terms, runtime selection and customer files. It
does not rewind database contents or restore an earlier database schema. Every
start performs the original actual source preflight. A release staged from the
operator workspace also retains its reviewed native column types and refuses a
changed schema before opening a seller listener.

## Start in the existing workspace

Set the endpoint, user and password environment variables named by the original
source configuration. Use the existing secret configuration for the host. Then:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge clickhouse-workspace \
  --state /private/clickhouse-workspace --port 8443
```

For native paid execution, add `--facilitator HTTPS_URL` and install the original
native payment dependencies from the distribution guide. The default remains
`CHALLENGE_ONLY`; source/schema preflight is real, but the seller does not execute
a paid query. The original loopback facilitator option is
`--allow-local-facilitator`, used only with an explicitly selected local URL.

Open the complete printed workspace URL. Save the real source and merchant plan,
review its native schema and every complete ordered payment option, and prepare
the merchant using the existing workflow. Under **Prepared merchants**:

1. Select the prepared merchant. Enter a stable release ID and descriptive label
   under **Publish and roll back retained releases**.
2. Choose **Stage selected merchant**. Staging is offline. It verifies and copies
   the original ten-file package and binds the existing native review to the
   retained release. Repeating the same ID with identical source, review schema,
   label and selected runtime reopens that same release. Changed work needs a new
   ID.
3. Choose **Open release controls**, then follow its private console link. Stop a
   direct workspace merchant first if one is running. The console owns the
   original retained-release child; its operations stay available in that console.
4. Select the staged release and review its route, complete payment alternatives,
   query contracts, source limits and retained package identity. Enter the change
   note and choose **Select this release**. Selection uses the original current
   generation and does not switch a running seller immediately.
5. Choose **Start selected** or **Restart selected**. Restart drains the original
   owned seller before launching the selected version. The console exposes the
   actual customer API, live OpenAPI, merchant operations and private availability
   controls returned by that instance.
6. After staging a second version, use the same comparison and restart workflow.
   **Select previous release** records the original rollback selection; **Restart
   selected** then serves that retained version. A failed new start leaves that
   version selected and the seller stopped, so the operator can select the earlier
   version and start it explicitly.

The workspace retains this ordinary SF82 store at
`STATE/merchant-releases`. **Close controls and drain seller** closes the original
console and the seller it owns. Closing the workspace also drains its owned
console/seller. Reopen the same workspace state to recover release inventory,
selection and history; reopening starts no seller automatically. Closing a browser
tab alone leaves the launching process running.

The workspace shows the release runtime before staging. It inherits the CLI's
seller port and facilitator selection. Retained children use the original
ClickHouse command's seller capacity of 64 and 60-second drain grace; source
concurrency, query/scan/result limits and request timeout remain those of the
retained original source and service. The direct-workspace
`--max-in-flight`/`--drain-grace-ms` options apply to its direct merchant.

## Original release CLI

The installed command is `starforge releases`. From a source checkout, use
`node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf82-seller-pilot/release-cli.mjs` in its place.
Prepare the original package first; the directory supplied below contains
`source.json`, `merchant-plan.json`, `service.json` and `client/`.

```sh
npx --no-install starforge releases init --store /private/clickhouse-releases
npx --no-install starforge releases stage \
  --store /private/clickhouse-releases --id transfers-v1 \
  --label 'Approved transfer query and terms' \
  --clickhouse-package /private/clickhouse-ready --port 8423
npx --no-install starforge releases console \
  --store /private/clickhouse-releases --port 8425
```

Add the selected `--facilitator HTTPS_URL` to **stage** for native execution; its
exact URL and local option are part of the retained runtime and release comparison.
This source form accepts no replacement handlers or upstream bindings.

The existing `list`, `inspect`, `diff`, `activate`, `rollback`, `status` and `run`
commands work on these releases. For a terminal-driven change, read `status` or
`diff` and pass the actual returned generation as `--expect`; do not substitute a
stale generation. `run` owns its foreground seller and Ctrl-C drains it. Stop an
existing manager in its own terminal or console before changing process ownership.

To stage another version, prepare a **new** ClickHouse directory from the revised
original source and plan, then stage it under a new release ID. The earlier retained
version is immutable. Direct bare-package staging verifies the original public and
typed input contract and uses fresh native preflight at each start. To retain the
workspace's prior native output-schema review as well, stage from that workspace.

## Customer delivery

Each retained release shown in the workspace has **Download retained client** and
**Download retained OpenAPI** actions. These continue to work after the former
prepared directory moves. The browser checks the response SHA-256 before saving.
The customer archive contains exactly:

| Member | Original product output |
| --- | --- |
| `openapi.json` | Prepared public API and exact payment alternatives |
| `client/seller-client.mjs` | Original generated JavaScript client |
| `client/seller-client.d.mts` | Its TypeScript declarations |
| `client/seller-openapi.json` | The exact OpenAPI bytes used by the generator |
| `client/package.json` | Original standalone client package |
| `client/README.md` | Its original usage guide |

SQL, source probes, private database configuration and credentials are excluded.
The prepared OpenAPI identifies the original preparation mode; the running
seller's **live OpenAPI** reports its actual current runtime mode. Use the original
merchant MCP client export below when a customer needs that exact running-instance
document. The existing generated-client/native buyer workflow and independent
customer spending cap remain unchanged.

## Bring the reviewed merchant into a fleet

Choose **Download fleet source** for a prepared merchant or **Download retained
fleet source** for an existing release. Both read the original verified package.
The retained form remains usable after the earlier prepared directory moves.

In the existing `/fleet.html` setup workbench, open the intended merchant and
registered source card, then choose **Import source JSON**. The source import
preserves that card's alias, replaces its source settings, and displays the
ordered native output-schema review. Review the original package path and
merchant host before exporting the fleet launch packet.

This private host file contains the existing native source alias fields:
`clickhousePackage`, optional `clickhouseColumnTypes`, and the selected
facilitator runtime. The fleet assigns its own fixed slot ports. Database
credentials remain in the merchant host environment. The original fleet setup,
stage, review, activation, operations, drain and rollback commands all consume
the same registered source and retained stores.

## Existing merchant MCP

Configure a new original MCP merchant against the host-selected package:

```sh
npx --no-install starforge merchant-mcp init \
  --dir /private/clickhouse-operator \
  --clickhouse-package /private/clickhouse-ready --seller-port 8423
npx --no-install starforge merchant-mcp serve \
  --config /private/clickhouse-operator/merchant-mcp.json
```

Use the original MCP bearer-token environment setup. Add `--facilitator HTTPS_URL`
to `init` when that is the selected runtime. An existing configuration can declare
another source alias with `clickhousePackage` and the original `runtime` fields.
When that package has a saved workspace review, retain its exact
`inspection.columnTypes` map as `clickhouseColumnTypes` on the same alias. The
original source inspector and stage operation validate it against the package,
include it in the execution identity, and require the same native types on start.
The `initializeMerchant` API accepts that same optional companion; aliases without
a saved map still perform the original native source preflight.
Arguments from an MCP client select that alias; they cannot select arbitrary host
paths, SQL or credentials.

Use the existing tools in order:

| Tool | Meaning for this merchant |
| --- | --- |
| `merchant_sources` | Verify the configured package, typed contracts, limits and full terms without connecting to the database |
| `merchant_stage` | Retain the original package under a new ID |
| `merchant_inspect` / `merchant_compare` | Read its exact digest and compare with the current selection |
| `merchant_activate` | Select that inspected digest using the current generation |
| `merchant_start` / `merchant_restart` | Open the original source and seller using the selected digest/generation and owned instance |
| `merchant_operations` | Return the original operations and private availability links for that instance |
| `merchant_catalog` | Read its actual health, complete offers and live OpenAPI |
| `merchant_client_export` | Produce the original five-file client from that running instance's OpenAPI in a new named customer directory |
| `merchant_rollback` | Select an inspected retained version using the original history and current generation |
| `merchant_stop` | Drain only the instance owned by this MCP process |

The MCP process and the browser console use the same original manager lock and
release history. They do not run the same merchant concurrently. To operate the
workspace's already-staged releases from an existing MCP configuration, set its
host `releaseStore` to the canonical `STATE/merchant-releases` directory and use
an existing private `exportsDirectory`; close the workspace-owned release console
before handing process ownership to MCP. Source aliases are needed only for new
staging. No new MCP tool or payment protocol is introduced.

## Retention and recovery details

The release adapter reads ten allowlisted original files with their existing
per-file limits and a 32 MiB aggregate limit. It verifies the native declaration,
original plan compiler, source/service bindings, full public OpenAPI and generated
client before copying. It rejects incomplete packages, changed bytes, symbolic
links and an output store nested inside the input package. The release manifest,
original offers and service bind the private copy by hashes. Inspection and
activation recheck those retained files; neither executes a query or starts a
listener.

Use the same installed compiler/client-generator version for preparation and
release operation. If the installation has changed since a package was prepared,
prepare a new directory from its retained source and plan with the current
installation. In the workspace, open its saved revision, run **Native review** and
**Prepare merchant**, then stage the resulting package. The previous working
directory and old release bytes remain unchanged. Preserve the matching original
installation with archived releases when moving them between hosts.

Mutable availability data lives separately under each release's
`clickhouse-runtime/availability`. The existing source preflight and merchant
shutdown close the source on failures. The SF82 manager's original readiness
handshake checks the exact retained offers/service and owns the started child.
The original release console supplies its own allowed navigation origin; private
operations API requests still require their own origin.

Keep the private release store, workspace revisions/reviews and original named
secret configuration in the host's existing backup process. If the live database
schema changes, reopen the saved source in the workspace, review the actual new
schema, and prepare/stage a new release. A column-type mismatch does not silently
rewrite a retained release. If a manager survives an interrupted controlling
session, the original status identifies its ownership; use that manager's existing
controls rather than launching a second seller.

Embedding applications may pass the host-only `env` option through
`startReleaseConsole` or `runActiveRelease`. It is copied into the original child
environment and is never stored in release JSON or exposed in browser responses.
The workspace also accepts an explicit `releaseRuntime` when supplied a custom
`nativeFactory`, because a JavaScript closure cannot be serialized into an
independent child. The normal workspace CLI derives this configuration from its
existing facilitator options. For a directly staged workspace-reviewed package,
the original `stageRelease` API accepts `clickhouseColumnTypes` alongside
`clickhousePackage`; the workspace supplies that map from its verified saved native
review.

# ClickHouse merchant operator workspace

Create and operate a merchant from the original [ClickHouse source and merchant plan](../README.md). The local browser joins private source selection, named-query authoring, native schema review, complete payment terms, retained merchant preparation, the original seller and operations, and generated customer downloads.

The workspace uses the existing ClickHouse HTTP source, scalar binder, merchant-plan compiler, preparer and seller lifecycle. Its saved revisions and folders can be reopened after the browser or launching terminal closes.

## Start the operator

Use the same Node runtime and optional native payment dependencies as the existing merchant installation. Linux's standard flock utility holds the original shared state lease. The standard tar utility creates the customer archive. There is no ClickHouse JavaScript driver or frontend build step.

Choose a private state directory outside the source checkout and outside every public web root. Newly created state directories use mode 0700; an existing directory must already have private permissions.

Set the three environment variables named by your source declaration in the launching terminal. For the supplied source example:

    export CLICKHOUSE_MERCHANT_URL='https://clickhouse.example/'
    export CLICKHOUSE_MERCHANT_USER='merchant_reader'
    read -rs -p 'ClickHouse password: ' CLICKHOUSE_MERCHANT_PASSWORD
    export CLICKHOUSE_MERCHANT_PASSWORD

Start with existing source and plan files:

    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/clickhouse/workspace/server.mjs \
      --state /srv/private/clickhouse-workspace \
      --source /srv/private/source.json \
      --plan /srv/private/merchant-plan.json

Alternatively, start with only the state directory and select both JSON files in the browser:

    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/clickhouse/workspace/server.mjs \
      --state /srv/private/clickhouse-workspace

Open the complete private URL printed by the command, including its fragment. The workspace listens on loopback; its source files and API require that private capability. Keep the launching terminal running while operating a merchant.

The original source account should have SELECT permission only on the data intended for sale. The adapter's SELECT wrapper and query limits complement those database permissions. HTTPS is the normal source transport. The explicit “Allow a loopback HTTP ClickHouse source” setting supports the original local development mode.

The browser receives the source's environment variable names, SQL and private probe values. Actual endpoint, account and password values stay in the server process; they are never returned by the workspace API or included in a customer download. Environment values are taken from the launching process. Restart the workspace with the same state directory after changing those values.

## 1. Select, author and save a revision

The **Source & offers** screen accepts the original source and merchant-plan schemas. Loading a file changes the current browser draft. **Save revision** validates both documents together through the native source reader and merchant-plan compiler and retains them as one immutable revision.

Use the connection fields to choose the database, environment references and native query budgets. Each named query has a private SELECT statement, typed parameter declarations, explicit output columns, a private preflight probe and result/deadline limits. Parameters use the original $name placeholders. The adapter supplies their native ClickHouse types and values separately.

The typed parameter JSON is the full existing contract. It supports string, integer, number, boolean and exact decimal declarations, their original bounds, enums, defaults and nullability. Decimal parameters require precision and scale. The **Native review** screen displays each compiled native type and every scalar constraint after a real preflight.

Public routes select one of these approved named queries. Set the route's HTTP method, path, service description, explicit public request example and descriptions for all public parameters. New routes start with an empty public example: private probe values are not copied into an offer. Supply an intentional public example before saving.

Each payment option preserves its complete scheme, network, asset, payTo, exact amount string, timeout and extra terms. The option list is ordered, and the up/down controls change the offered order. Amount fields never pass through a JavaScript number. A route can supply its own complete option array instead of inheriting the shared array; both are displayed in the compiled review.

The **Complete native documents** section supports direct source and plan JSON editing. Apply those documents to the form before saving. The original server-side compiler remains authoritative for all fields and validation.

Saved history retains the source and plan together. Opening an earlier revision selects it without changing a running merchant. Edits become a new revision when saved. An unchanged source/plan pair reuses its existing revision and label. Concurrent browser windows compare the editor's adopted revision before a save or selection; an inventory refresh cannot advance that editor base. Refresh and reopen when another window has moved saved work.

## 2. Review the real source and prepare

Choose **Review native source** after saving. The original adapter opens the selected ClickHouse account, reads the native server version and performs its zero-row preflight for every named query. The workspace displays actual native result types, compiled parameter types and the configured scan, memory and deadline budgets.

The review is retained with the exact source/plan revision. A private preview takes explicit typed input values and executes the selected approved query using the same source adapter. Results preserve exact non-null ClickHouse text and JSON null. The original row cap and truncation indicator remain visible; a preview is a single-request snapshot.

Review every compiled route and every complete payment option. Acknowledging that review and choosing **Prepare merchant** invokes the original offline preparer. It creates:

| Retained merchant member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| source.json | Private approved SQL, probes, environment references and route bindings |
| merchant-plan.json | The reviewed public route and payment declarations |
| service.json / bindings.json | Original compiled seller configuration |
| openapi.json | Original public API description |
| client/ | Original generated JavaScript client, declarations and customer guide |

The containing workspace record keeps the selected revision, native review and exact prepared files together. The native merchant folder is published only after preparation completes. Its full path is shown in **Prepared merchants**.

Repeated preparation of the same revision and review returns the retained merchant. If the process ended during offline preparation, the screen identifies that unfinished preparation and offers **Resume preparation**. That action rebuilds only its unpublished private copy from the same retained inputs, then publishes the complete folder. If publication already completed, it validates that same folder and finishes removing the consumed preparation intent. It does not perform a customer request or settlement.

If native result types change after review, a private preview or merchant start reports that change. Review the saved revision again and prepare a new merchant from that new review. After updating the installed SDK, the same fresh preparation path also creates outputs with the current compiler.

## 3. Operate the original merchant

Open a retained merchant to inspect its complete terms. **Start merchant** verifies its retained files, performs the original fresh native preflight and opens the existing SF30 seller and operations interfaces. A workspace owns one active merchant at a time.

The screen exposes the original customer API, OpenAPI, operations, availability and availability controls. Those URLs belong to the running original merchant. **Stop merchant** waits for its existing drain lifecycle, closes its operations and ClickHouse source, and keeps the prepared folder available.

The workspace binds its actual loopback origin to the original operations listener's navigation interface. An explicit click opens the original HTML page with only that origin as the referrer; the private URL fragment is excluded. Operations API and export reads retain the original same-origin policy.

Without a facilitator, the original seller runs in CHALLENGE_ONLY mode and responds with HTTP 402. To operate the existing paid path, start the workspace with the original native payment dependencies and facilitator:

    node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/clickhouse/workspace/server.mjs \
      --state /srv/private/clickhouse-workspace \
      --facilitator https://facilitator.example \
      --seller-port 8423 \
      --operations-port 8424

The original HTTPFacilitatorClient and native seller factory handle the payment path, including the existing Stellar scheme. Payment accounts, assets and networks are the explicit terms from the reviewed plan. The workspace does not substitute its own verifier, signer, settlement semantics or payment policy.

The original explicit local facilitator mode is available with both --facilitator and --allow-local-facilitator. Native ports default to dynamically allocated loopback ports; --seller-port and --operations-port select fixed ports. --port selects the operator browser port, default 8443. --max-in-flight and --drain-grace-ms pass through to this direct seller lifecycle.

## 4. Publish, upgrade and roll back

**Publish and roll back retained releases** connects the selected prepared folder
to the existing SF82 merchant release store. Enter a release ID and label, then
choose **Stage selected merchant**. The original release adapter verifies and
retains the source, full typed input/payment contract, customer files and this
workspace's saved native result-column types. Repeating an identical stage
reopens the same release; different source or runtime needs a new ID.

Choose **Open release controls** and follow the private console link. The
original release console compares routes, complete payment alternatives, named
query contracts and limits. **Select this release** records the original
generation-checked selection. **Start selected** opens it; **Restart selected**
drains the running original seller before starting the selected version. The
running instance exposes its original customer API, live OpenAPI, operations and
availability controls. **Select previous release** followed by **Restart selected**
serves a retained version again.

The release store is `STATE/merchant-releases`. It remains usable when a former
prepared input folder moves. Downloads beside each retained release use that
verified private copy and the original six-file customer archive. The release
console owns retained child launches; stop a direct workspace merchant before
opening it, and close the console before returning to direct starts. **Close
controls and drain seller** closes its original owned processes while preserving
all releases and selection history.

The release runtime inherits the original CLI's seller port and facilitator.
Its child uses the original ClickHouse command's capacity of 64 and 60-second
drain grace. The source's separate query/scan/concurrency limits remain unchanged.
ClickHouse data stays live: rollback restores a service definition, not database
history. Every launch performs the original actual preflight; a changed native
column type fails before the retained workspace release opens a listener.

Use [Retained ClickHouse merchant releases](../../../sf82-seller-pilot/CLICKHOUSE_RELEASES.md)
for the complete console, CLI, existing MCP, customer-delivery and recovery flow.

## Deliver the customer client

**Download customer client** returns a gzip tar archive containing exactly the original public OpenAPI plus the five generated client files. **Download OpenAPI** returns the same public description separately. The browser checks the completed download bytes before saving.

The customer archive contains no private source declaration, SQL, probes, merchant plan file or credentials. The public OpenAPI deliberately includes the reviewed public examples and payment information. Check those public fields during offer review.

Extract the archive into a customer application and follow its generated client/README.md. It uses the existing buyer runtime and original response/result behavior described in the [installed ClickHouse merchant/customer guide](../../../distribution/README.md#prepare-and-operate-a-clickhouse-merchant). The workspace's customer API link opens the same merchant's original developer portal.

## Reopen and retain work

Close the browser whenever needed; the process and active merchant continue in the launching terminal. Reopening the same private URL restores saved work. Unsaved form edits live only in the open page.

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM in the launching terminal drains the original merchant before releasing the state lease. Later, run the same workspace command with --state and without --source/--plan to reopen its current revision, reviews and merchant history. Restarting does not automatically start a merchant or repeat a private preview. A last-run entry from an interrupted previous session is shown as historical context.

Only one workspace process can own a state directory. The reused native flock lease releases when its owning file description closes or its process exits; it has no stale-PID deletion or manual unlock race. Stop the owning workspace before opening that same state directory elsewhere.

Keep the entire private state directory for backup or migration. Its revisions/ directory contains immutable source/plan pairs and their retained native reviews; prepared/ contains the original complete merchant folders and original availability state; staging/ contains unpublished offline preparation work; merchant-releases/ contains the original immutable SF82 releases, selection history and retained per-release availability. Complete merchant folders remain usable with the existing clickhouse/start.mjs --directory command after the workspace has stopped.

## Programmatic composition

model.mjs exports createClickHouseWorkspace. server.mjs exports startClickHouseWorkspace and main. The model accepts stateDirectory, optional initial sourceFile/planFile, the existing nativeFactory, native seller ports/lifecycle options and an environment object. An embedding with a custom nativeFactory supplies releaseRuntime with the explicit original facilitator/port options when it wants retained child launches; the normal CLI derives these values from its existing options. The host-only environment also reaches the original release child without being stored or returned to the browser.

The server's loopback capability API exposes state, saved revision selection, save, native review, private preview, prepare, retained release inspection, run, stop and customer export. It also stages a selected prepared merchant through the original release store and opens/closes the original release console. State changes use the original atomic file helper and one process-owned native lease. Browser mutations carry explicit revision, review, release or run identity; they do not submit arbitrary source paths, credential values, shell commands or replacement payment behavior.

# ClickHouse merchant

Expose an approved ClickHouse query through the original Stellar Forge merchant and deliver its result with the original customer client. This adapter provides native database preflight, typed request admission, exact text results, bounded analytical queries, a retained merchant folder, and the existing seller operations console. It uses Node's existing SF30 HTTP transport; no ClickHouse JavaScript driver is required.

The payment path is the maintained SF30 seller and native x402 SDK. The input rules, public offer compiler, customer SDK exporter, seller lifecycle and operations UI are reused from the original implementations. This folder adds the ClickHouse source adapter and its onboarding commands.

## Connect an existing analytical source

Use a dedicated database account with `SELECT` on the approved tables or views. Keep field/row authorization in those views and account grants. A caller-selected account filter is a query parameter, not an authenticated tenant identity. For customer-specific data, use the existing application's authorization or an appropriately restricted source view.

For example, the database administrator can grant an existing merchant principal access to one approved view:

```sql
GRANT SELECT ON analytics.approved_transfers TO merchant_user;
```

The adapter sends fixed `SELECT` wrappers using ClickHouse's HTTP interface. ClickHouse automatically applies `readonly=2` to ordinary non-POST HTTP requests when the account has no stricter setting. That mode still permits settings changes and some other commands; the database grants remain the access boundary. See [ClickHouse query permissions](https://clickhouse.com/docs/concepts/features/configuration/settings/permissions-for-queries).

Make the three environment variables named in the private source configuration available through the host's existing secret setup. `endpointEnv` resolves to the HTTPS ClickHouse HTTP endpoint, ending in `/`; an existing reverse-proxy prefix is supported. Credentials use `X-ClickHouse-User` and `X-ClickHouse-Key` headers, and the database uses `X-ClickHouse-Database`. Credentials never enter buyer requests, public offers, generated clients, source inspection or response errors. The ClickHouse server and its own operator logs retain their normal database behavior.

For a local database, set `allowLocal: true` and use an explicitly selected `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`, `http://localhost:PORT/` or IPv6 loopback endpoint. HTTPS uses Node's normal certificate verification. No caller can choose the upstream endpoint or headers.

The [example source](examples/source.json) and [merchant plan](examples/merchant-plan.json) are usable starting documents. The optional [seed SQL](examples/seed.sql) creates a small in-memory demonstration dataset. Its rows are demonstration data; they are not Goldsky exports or chain transactions. Run it only in the selected local demonstration database. Replace the conspicuous demonstration payment identifiers in the plan with the actual complete terms before a customer deployment.

## Declare the product query

A source is `stellar-forge.clickhouse-source.v1`. Each named query supplies trusted SQL, explicit projected column names, parameter declarations, row/byte/deadline limits and a `probe` object. The probe provides actual valid values for startup metadata preflight. It stays in the private source file.

SQL templates use the shared SF30 `$name` parameter notation. The adapter translates each declared parameter into a native ClickHouse `{name:Type}` placeholder. Values travel separately as native `param_name` HTTP parameters, with ClickHouse Escaped serialization followed by URL encoding. SQL literals, comments and heredocs are retained. Every declared parameter must appear in the template, and undeclared placeholders or multiple statements are rejected. Alias projected columns to simple unique identifiers when source columns use spaces or punctuation. ClickHouse parses the actual query during preflight; the template linter is not a SQL sandbox.

| Input declaration | Native parameter | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `String` | Original length bounds and enum; valid Unicode; NUL rejected. Tabs, newlines, quotes and backslashes survive the native escaped-parameter encoding. |
| `integer` | `Int64` | Canonical signed 64-bit decimal text, or a safe integer JSON number. Use text for values outside JavaScript's safe integer range. |
| `number` | `Float64` | Finite JavaScript number, or original numeric text; ordinary binary floating-point conversion applies. |
| `boolean` | `Bool` | JSON booleans or the original `"true"` / `"false"` strings. |
| `decimal` | `Decimal(precision, scale)` | Exact decimal string; explicit precision 1–76 and scale 0–precision. Integer overflow or excess nonzero fractional digits are rejected before payment. Trailing fractional zeroes may be accepted without changing value. |
| Any type with `nullable: true` | `Nullable(...)` | JSON null is distinct from a literal string. The original default and enum rules still apply. |

The original exact-decimal validator enforces minimum, maximum and numeric enum comparisons without converting through JavaScript numbers. A `Decimal(20, 0)` parameter with bounds `0` and `18446744073709551615` can represent a full UInt64 cursor; the example uses this for `after_record_id`. Use `Decimal(p, p)` when no nonzero integer digits are permitted.

There may be 1–64 named queries, 1–64 projected columns and up to 48 parameters per query. The original transport's **8,192-character encoded URL budget** covers SQL, settings and all parameter values together. Admission checks that actual encoded request before payment. Very large SQL templates or long encoded values must be reduced to fit this transport contract.

The example uses a two-part `(ledger, record_id)` cursor and a stable ordering. For the next page, pass both values from the same last delivered row. This preserves later records within that ledger. Keep the other filters unchanged. Each call reads the current database; separate calls do not share a frozen snapshot. An immutable source view or retained dataset product is appropriate when the application requires frozen pagination.

## Prepare, inspect and start

Run these commands from `stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk` in the installed original source/runtime:

```sh
node clickhouse/prepare.mjs \
  --source /private/clickhouse-draft/source.json \
  --plan /private/clickhouse-draft/merchant-plan.json \
  --directory /private/clickhouse-ready

node clickhouse/start.mjs --directory /private/clickhouse-ready --inspect

node clickhouse/start.mjs --directory /private/clickhouse-ready \
  --port 8423 --operations-port 8424
```

Preparation is offline and creates a new private directory. It retains `source.json`, the reviewed `merchant-plan.json`, the original `service.json` and `bindings.json`, plus the original exported `openapi.json` and complete `client/` folder. Files use owner-only permissions. The source's credentials remain environment references. Move the entire folder and supply the same named environment variables on the destination host.

An `INCOMPLETE` marker remains if the process is interrupted before preparation finishes; the launcher refuses that partial folder. Prepare again into a new directory from the retained source and plan. Existing destinations are never overwritten. For an intentional query or price change, prepare a new directory, review it, then switch the existing operator-managed launch configuration.

`--inspect` authenticates to the actual database, obtains its version, and runs each query with `LIMIT 0` and its private probe. It prints actual native column types, the public parameter contract and configured limits, then closes. Every normal start performs this same schema preflight before opening the seller. During delivery, a changed native result schema is rejected with `QUERY_SCHEMA_CHANGED`.

The default launch serves the original HTTP 402 challenges. Enable the maintained payment path using the original installed x402 dependencies and your configured facilitator:

```sh
node clickhouse/start.mjs --directory /private/clickhouse-ready \
  --facilitator https://facilitator.example
```

The original seller binds to loopback for the host's existing HTTPS ingress. Startup prints the merchant URL, API docs, OpenAPI, health/readiness and operations URLs. `--no-operations` omits the operations listener. `--availability-dir` retains the original availability controls; `--max-in-flight` and `--drain-grace-ms` configure the original seller's lifecycle. SIGINT/SIGTERM drain that lifecycle and close the source. An explicitly selected local facilitator can use `--allow-local-facilitator` with an HTTP URL on `127.0.0.1`.

## Deliver through the existing buyer

Give the customer the generated `client/` folder and public API specification. Keep the source SQL and database credentials with the merchant. The exported module supports the original SF88 Node Buyer and its existing operator workspace; see [the maintained Node buyer guide](../../sf88-operator-buyer-cli/node/README.md) and the generated client's own README.

```js
import { Buyer } from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/buyer/node';
import { createSellerClient } from './client/seller-client.mjs';

const buyer = new Buyer({
  runtimeDirectory: '/opt/starforge/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf88-operator-buyer-cli',
  stateDirectory: '/private/customer/buyer-state',
  operatorProfile: '/private/customer/operator-profile.json',
});
const client = createSellerClient({ buyer });
const result = await client.call('transfers', {
  body: { account: 'merchant-demo', after_ledger: '0', after_record_id: '0', minimum_amount: '0' },
}, { intentId: 'transfer-page-001', maxAtomic: '10000', acceptIndex: 0 });
const page = await result.json();
console.log(page.rows);
```

Use the actual configured public route, accepted payment option and an independent customer cap. The original buyer owns approval, durable reservation, signing, response saving and financial finalization. The ClickHouse adapter adds none of those mechanisms. The generated client also exports `buildRequest` for the maintained SF31 transport or another existing buyer integration.

Successful query responses use `stellar-forge.clickhouse-result.v1`: ordered `columns`, actual `columnTypes`, object `rows`, `rowCount`, `truncated`, `valueEncoding: "clickhouse-text"`, `nullEncoding: "json-null"` and `snapshot: "single-request"`. **Every non-null cell is a string**, including booleans, integers, decimals, timestamps and composite values. SQL null is JSON null. Decode a column according to its native type when your application needs a typed value; do not turn large integers or exact amounts into JavaScript numbers.

ClickHouse's `JSONCompactStrings` representation can spell SQL NULL as a printable string. The adapter requests an independent native `isNull` flag for each projected column in the same statement, then removes those private flags from the response. A literal `"ᴺᵁᴸᴸ"` or `"\\N"` therefore stays a string. Invalid UTF-8 output is refused by the original strict transport; project arbitrary binary data explicitly with ClickHouse `hex` or `base64` when that is the approved API contract.

## Query cost and operational behavior

| Limit | Default / allowed range | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query `maxRows` | 100 / 1–1,000 | Native `LIMIT maxRows + 1`; one sentinel determines `truncated`. |
| Query `maxBytes` | 512 KiB / 1–896 KiB | Native result-byte setting, bounded transport and final JSON-byte check. Oversized results fail; no clipped successful JSON. |
| Query `timeoutMs` | 1,500 ms / 50–30,000 ms | Original HTTP deadline plus native `max_execution_time`. |
| Source `maxInFlight` | 8 / 1–64 | Source admission and original transport capacity. |
| Source `maxThreads` | 2 / 1–8 | Native per-query parallelism. |
| Source `maxMemoryBytes` | 256 MiB / 1 MiB–2 GiB | Native per-query memory setting. |
| Source `maxRowsToRead` | 1,000,000 / 1–1,000,000,000 | Native scan-row setting and final native statistics check. |
| Source `maxBytesToRead` | 64 MiB / 1 KiB–2 GiB | Native scan-byte setting and final native statistics check. |

The adapter requests `wait_end_of_query=1` and validates the complete JSON response, including native column metadata. It forces result, read and timeout overflow modes to `throw`, so its imposed limits do not inherit a profile's partial-result `break` mode. Native scan statistics are required and compared with the source budget; a completed block that exceeds it is refused with `QUERY_SCAN_LIMIT`. This check cannot undo work already performed by the database. Query limits can be checked in blocks or at cooperative execution points; configure the account's resource profile for its actual workload. If the account restricts setting changes, permit these specific settings in that existing profile before startup.

`cancel_http_readonly_queries_on_client_close=1` requests native cancellation when the original transport closes a read request. The source also cancels active HTTP lifetimes during close and waits for those local operations to finish. There is no automatic query retry or query queue. Public errors distinguish invalid input (422), source capacity (429), request timeout (504), and unavailable/invalid database delivery (503), without exposing native SQL error bodies.

Primary protocol references: [HTTP parameters, headers and response behavior](https://clickhouse.com/docs/concepts/features/interfaces/http), [JSONCompactStrings](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/formats/JSON/JSONCompactStrings), [disconnect cancellation](https://clickhouse.com/docs/reference/settings/session-settings/other#cancel_http_readonly_queries_on_client_close), and [settings for read-only clients](https://clickhouse.com/docs/clickstack/managing/production).

[Goldsky Turbo supports ClickHouse sinks](https://docs.goldsky.com/turbo-pipelines/quickstart). A customer who already owns or is entitled to the relevant sink can expose an approved downstream view with this adapter: confirm the actual view and distribution rights, supply the merchant's SELECT account, choose the exact public query/terms, prepare the merchant, and hand over the generated client. This uses the customer's database endpoint and does not require another ingestion engine or a change to an existing commercial offer.

## Native integration exercised

The complete local flow used official ClickHouse **26.8.24.9**, original SF30/SF31, native x402 **2.28.0**, and the original generated client. Actual database output preserved UInt64 `18446744073709551615`, ledger `9007199254740993`, amount `123456789012345678901234567890.1234567`, microsecond timestamps, escaped Unicode, SQL null, a literal null marker, and `Decimal(4,4)`. Composite pagination retained the remaining row in the same ledger; the prepared source reopened with matching output.

The native merchant/buyer exercise made one unsigned request and one signed-envelope retry through an explicitly controlled local facilitator, delivered HTTP 200 with the exact database result, and rejected excess decimal scale before additional verification or settlement. The facilitator deliberately returned `LOCAL_ACCEPTANCE_NO_CHAIN`; the original buyer correctly classified its financial outcome as `PAYMENT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` / `INVALID_TRANSACTION_HASH`. This validates the database/merchant/buyer integration without claiming a blockchain transfer. The retained real testnet payment journey elsewhere in Stellar Forge remains the chain-payment evidence.
